outline.description:
"Large language models today reach tens of billions of parameters.
Even shallow learning signals consume extraordinary amounts
of GPU RAM when every weight is updated.
Existing inference-only quantisation packages
cannot be trained because algebraic derivatives explode
with precision loss.
QLoRa addresses both constraints:
and shows that freezing a well-trained base
in very low precision does not deteriorate accuracy
when adapters receive gradients through it."

"Before defining QLoRa it is helpful
to formalise blockwise k-bit
quantisation\nand low-rank adapters.
Blockwise schemes split tensors so
outliers fit into narrow bins,
and LoRa replaces expensive dense updates
with two small rank projections."

"QLoRa freezes a heavily quantified backbone
and learns only tiny rank adapters.
Gradients propagate through tape-held
low-bit tensors during forward
automatically converting them back
to full precision before multiplying.
No weight update occurs in the backbone;
it absorbs information solely via its adapters."
